Correct reading nu=(6,5,4,2), pi=(9,5,3) reproduces their published untuned 6>5 exactly as 2*3 > 1*5; brute force over all pi in Z^3 with |pi|=17 under the printed labelling finds no reading giving 6>5

Speyer's L-log-concavity quantifies over functions on the weight lattice Z^n valued in LR/skep counts; my July object is the coefficient sequence of c_gamma(t) in Z[t] indexed by t-degree. Different estimands; no t anywhere in 2601.05007. Speyer does NOT cover the chain regime.

even granting a bridge: chain regime c_{gamma(L)}(t) = [n-L]_t is the all-ones sequence, so log-concavity is the EQUALITY 1*1>=1*1. 10/10 chain-regime probe entries all-ones; 12/24 for (3,3,*,0); 44/70 overall. The '46/46' count does not reproduce (probe has 34 entries in chain u (3,3,*,0)).

children.approach: PROVED: (1) one-box-per-column <=> kappa_i >= nu_{i+1}; (2) on that locus s_{nu/kappa} = prod_i h_{nu_i-kappa_i}, so by Pieri c^nu_{kappa,lambda} = K_{lambda,nu-kappa}; (3) the value depends only on (lambda, nu-kappa) and by HMMS's own converse every Kostka number arises -- the label nu is redundant. Hence NO instance of their proved LR corollary is not a Kostka statement. Verified: 927 shapes 0 mismatches, 1019 triples 0 violations, 0 multi-valued classes.

Passes 16 untuned positive controls (normalized Schur, HMMS Thm 3) AND fails correctly on 3 negative controls, one per condition.

children.approach: PROVED: if every vertex weight in row i is homogeneous of degree 1 in (x_i,y_i), then every monomial of Z has deg_{x_i} + deg_{y_i} = m, so supp(Z) lies on the graph {(alpha, m*1 - alpha)} in Z^{2n}. Verified on every monomial of every Z computed.

REFUTED by my own test: 'every non-monomial Z in the two-variable-per-row setting fails M-convexity' is FALSE -- over 60 random non-free-fermion weight families, 441 of 769 non-monomial partition functions DO have M-convex support. So the obstruction is specific to the free-fermion locus, not a formal consequence of the row-degree lemma.
children.reason: refuted computationally; the structural argument I sketched from the row-degree lemma does not close, because the x-support is not confined to a single total-degree level (1/769 cases)

children.approach: Q177 ANSWERED NO. Enumerated 1554 homogeneous nonneg free-fermion weight families (coeffs in {0,1,2}); tested 40 across all boundaries for (n,m) in {(2,2),(2,3)}: 760 nonzero Z, 352 non-monomial, of which 252 NOT Lorentzian (170 fail (L2) M-convexity, 82 fail (L3)) and 100 Lorentzian -- the 100 all being products of nonneg linear forms, hence degenerate. Witness: (a1,a2,b1,b2,c1,c2)=(x,y,y,x,2x,y) gives Z = 2 x1 x2 (x1 y2 + x2 y1), whose support {(1,0,0,1),(0,1,1,0)} differs by (1,-1,-1,1) and is not M-convex.

CONCLUSION: the 238-vs-640 bibliographic gap is an OBSTRUCTION, not an absence. Free-fermion six-vertex partition functions are generically not Lorentzian, so the edge I proposed to build in July does not exist. The Schur case survives because the five-vertex model is NOT homogeneous per row (four weights equal 1) -- its homogeneity comes from the boundary, so the x-degree is a genuine statistic with permutohedral (M-convex) support. That property does not deform.
